text: 🇲🇽🌎 Venezuela was hit by two earthquakes. Mexico's rescuers were on a plane the same day. "Our solidarity with the people of Venezuela. Today a team from the Ministry of National Defense — rescuers and medical personnel — departs for Venezuela." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Two quakes, magnitude 7.2 and 7.5, struck Venezuela on June 24. Mexico dispatched a SEDENA team of rescuers and medics the next morning, with more to follow as needed. Solidarity, no conditions attached.

🚨🇲🇽 52 dead in ICE custody. Mexico is sending diplomatic notes — and taking the cases to the Inter-American Commission. "There are issues where we don't agree. One of them, which worries us and occupies us, is the death of Mexicans in ICE detention centers. We've been raising it with the ambassador and sending the diplomatic notes required." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Human Rights Watch and Physicians for Human Rights count 52 deaths in ICE custody under Trump's second term — a 140% jump in the death rate. Mexico's consuls were ordered to review detention conditions; the cases are headed to the CIDH.

🇲🇽💵 TRUMP BET ON FEAR. MEXICAN MIGRANTS SENT MORE MONEY ANYWAY

Despite deportation raids and a proposed US tax on transfers, remittances to Mexico rose 2.6% over the first four months of 2026, per Banxico — $14.166 billion in the first quarter alone, up from $13.966 billion a year earlier. April pulled in $4.978 billion, +3.7% year-on-year. Washington keeps trying to weaponize the people who do its hardest work; the lifeline they send home only got bigger.

🚨🇲🇽 FOUR US AGENTS ENTERED MEXICO WITHOUT PERMISSION — TWO DIED

Asked whether PAN governor Maru Campos is a CIA informant, Sheinbaum said there's no evidence — then noted the PAN's long record of "subordination" to Washington. The case she pointed to is bigger than gossip: an FGR investigation into four US agents who entered Mexico without complying with its national-security law, two of them now dead. "It's not for the government of Mexico to judge," she said — the prosecutors decide, on Mexican terms.

🔥🇲🇽 THE OLD PRI MACHINE COMES DUE — 10 WARRANTS FOR SELLING TEACHER JOBS

State of Mexico prosecutors issued 10 arrest warrants over the irregular sale of around 300 teaching positions — including at least 70 paying more than 120,000 pesos a month. Among those already detained: Óscar N, who ran administration under PRI ex-governor Alfredo Del Mazo. The jobs that should have gone to teachers were auctioned off; the people who auctioned them are now in handcuffs.

🇲🇽⚽ MEXICO MARCHES INTO THE KNOCKOUTS UNBEATEN — A FIRST IN 18 WORLD CUPS

El Tri beat the Czech Republic 3-0 at the Azteca to win Group A with three wins, nine points and not a single goal conceded — the first time in 18 World Cup appearances Mexico has cleared the group stage perfect. Mateo Chávez, Julián Quiñones and Álvaro Fidalgo scored. Guillermo Ochoa took an ovation from more than 80,000 at home in his sixth World Cup. The country hosting the tournament is winning on its own pitch.

NPR/KCUR: Trump says the U.S. doesn't need a trade deal with its neighbors. Farm groups push hard for renewal
June 24, 2026 | 🟡

Trump dares Mexico and Canada to walk; US farm groups are the ones "pushing hard" to keep USMCA alive before the July 1 review. The loudest opponents of the pressure campaign are American.

Peterson Institute's math: Texas alone shipped ~$42.6B in petroleum to Mexico and Canada in 2025, and Trump-leaning export states stand to lose the most if the deal dies. Termination is "highly unlikely," PIIE notes — because Trump makes "heavy demands" while "offering no concessions."

• Trump: the U.S. "doesn't need a trade deal with its neighbors"
• PIIE: the risk "is not zero" — heavy demands, no concessions offered

LATIN TIMES: El Chapo writes handwritten letters requesting extradition to Mexico
June 25, 2026 | 🟡

The LA Times calls the five handwritten letters "bizarre" and a "mystery." Strip the framing and it's simpler: a man convicted in a Brooklyn court, held in a US supermax, is asking — pro se, by hand — to be sent back to his own country, citing "cruel punishment."

Mexico extradited him; the US tried him in New York. A request to be returned home reads as "bizarre" only if you assume US custody is where a Mexican national naturally belongs. Judge Cogan dismissed the letters as making "no sense."

• Guzmán requested an "extradition release back to Mexico"
• He cited "cruel punishment" handed down in Brooklyn
